title: 〜とき (tense inside the とき clause)
meaning: "When…" — the tense of the verb before とき shows whether the とき action is complete relative to the main action.
simpleExplanation: とき means "when", but the form of the verb before it tells you the order of events. Dictionary form + とき: the main action happens BEFORE or DURING the とき action (日本へ行くとき、お土産を買った = I bought souvenirs on the way, before arriving). た-form + とき: the main action happens AFTER the とき action is finished (日本へ行ったとき、京都を見た = after I got to Japan, I saw Kyoto). The tense at the end of the sentence shows when the whole thing happened; the form before とき only shows which came first.
whenUsed: Any time you say "when": daily routines (寝るとき歯を磨く), past stories (子供のとき), instructions (分からないときは聞いてください). The dictionary/た distinction matters most with movement and change verbs: 行く, 来る, 帰る, 着く, 出る, 入る.
formation: V-dictionary + とき: main action before or during (家を出るとき、鍵をかける)
V-た + とき: main action after the とき action is completed (家に帰ったとき、手を洗う)
V-ている + とき: during an ongoing action (テレビを見ているとき)
い-adjective + とき, な-adjective + なとき, Noun + のとき: 忙しいとき, 暇なとき, 子供のとき
The final verb sets the overall tense; the とき clause is relative to it

examples.ja: 日本へ行くとき、空港でお土産を買った。
examples.reading: にほんへ いくとき、くうこうで おみやげを かった。
examples.en: When I was going to Japan, I bought souvenirs at the airport (before arriving).
examples.note: Dictionary form: the buying happened before arrival (at the departure airport).

examples.ja: 日本へ行ったとき、京都を見に行った。
examples.reading: にほんへ いったとき、きょうとを みに いった。
examples.en: When I went to Japan, I went to see Kyoto (after arriving).
examples.note: た-form: the sightseeing happened after arriving in Japan.

examples.ja: 子供のとき、よく川で泳いだ。
examples.reading: こどもの とき、よく かわで およいだ。
examples.en: When I was a child, I often swam in the river.
examples.note: Noun + のとき: a period of life.

examples.ja: 家を出るとき、電気を消すのを忘れないでください。
examples.reading: いえを でるとき、でんきを けすのを わすれないでください。
examples.en: When you leave the house, don't forget to turn off the lights.
examples.note: You turn off the lights before actually going out: dictionary form + とき.

examples.ja: 駅に着いたとき、電車はもう出ていた。
examples.reading: えきに ついたとき、でんしゃは もう でていた。
examples.en: When I got to the station, the train had already left.
examples.note: た-form: the arriving was complete when the speaker saw the train gone.

similarGrammar.difference: たら also means "when" for the future, but always with the order "A finished, then B". とき can express both orders.
間に means "during the time that" and needs a continuing state or action. とき is a point or period "when".
場合 is "in the case that", used for possibilities and rules. とき is for real times and events.

commonMistakes.wrong: 家に帰るとき、手を洗います。(meaning: after getting home)
commonMistakes.right: 家に帰ったとき、手を洗います。
commonMistakes.why: Washing hands happens after you get home, so the completed た-form is needed. 帰るとき would mean "on the way home".

commonMistakes.wrong: 日本へ行ったとき、空港でお土産を買いました。(bought at the home airport before leaving)
commonMistakes.right: 日本へ行くとき、空港でお土産を買いました。
commonMistakes.why: The buying was before arrival, so the dictionary form is required, even though the whole sentence is past.

commonMistakes.wrong: 暇のとき、映画を見ます。
commonMistakes.right: 暇なとき、映画を見ます。
commonMistakes.why: な-adjectives take な before とき; の is for nouns (子供のとき).

usageNotes: Verbs of state (いる, ある, 分かる, 忙しい) usually take the dictionary form regardless of time: 日本にいるとき, 分からないとき.
With verbs that take time (食べる, 読む), dictionary form + とき means "while": ご飯を食べるとき、テレビを見ない.
〜たとき can be shortened to 〜たら in casual speech for past sequences, but とき is the form tested for the order of events.
jlptTips: Look for movement verbs (行く, 来る, 帰る, 着く, 出る) before the blank. Ask: was the main action done before or after arriving? Before → dictionary form; after → た-form.
The final verb's tense is a distractor: 買った at the end does not mean the とき verb must be 行った. Decide by the order of events, not by the sentence's tense.
